title: Contribution workflow, RFCs, and sunset policy for tokens & components
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket codifies a lightweight governance playbook for the Redwood design system: how contributors propose changes (tokens, components, charts), how we review and approve via RFCs, and the formal deprecation/sunset path for tokens and components. Goal is predictable change, clear ownership, low-friction contributions, and safe removals that minimize customer disruption.

Scope:
- Visual/semantic tokens (colors, spacing, typography)
- Primitive components (Button, Input, Table, Chart primitives) and composed components (DataTable, ChartPanel)
- Design tokens JSON/spec, Storybook entries, snapshot/tests, migration helpers

Contribution guidelines (developer-friendly):
- Small PR philosophy: prefer incremental changes under 200 lines for tokens and <3 logical changes per PR for components.
- PR template: every contribution must fill the DS PR template (link to repo template), including: motivation, screenshots/recorded interaction, backwards-compat notes, token map if applicable, and playbook checklist.
- Required artifacts for non-trivial changes: Storybook example, unit test, visual snapshot, and a short migration note (if changing token names/semantics).
- Ownership: set CODEOWNERS to notify the DS team and the component owner. If no owner exists, the design team lead is required approver.

Review checklist (what reviewers must verify):
- Design sign-off: a designer has reviewed visuals, spacing, and token intent.
- Accessibility: keyboard focus, semantic HTML, ARIA roles where relevant, color contrast check with tokens referenced.
- Token hygiene: new tokens must follow token-naming conventions, include rationale, and avoid duplicating existing tokens.
- Theming/back-compat: confirm behavior under Redwood themes (light/dark/high-contrast) and that default behavior is preserved unless intentionally changed.
- Performance: no obvious render/alloc regressions for high-frequency components (Button, Input, Table).
- Docs & examples: Storybook examples demonstrate the public surface and edge cases; migration steps included for breaking changes.
- Tests: unit tests for logic, visual snapshots for appearance, and a note describing which bundles/codepaths are affected.

RFC process (when to open an RFC):
- RFC required for any change that meets at least one of: token rename or semantic change, breaking API change, removing a component, or significant performance optimization affecting runtime behavior.
- RFC stages: Draft -> Reviewed -> Accepted -> Scheduled -> Implemented -> Deprecated (if applicable).
- Timeline expectations: 3 business days for initial review comments, 7–14 days for design+eng alignment before 'Accepted' or 'Needs Revision'. Urgent fixes are allowed but must be retroactively RFC'd within one week.
- Reviewers: DS design lead, owning engineers, accessibility lead (if applicable), and a release manager for scheduling.

Deprecation & sunset policy (safe removals):
- Deprecation Announcement: when a token/component is marked deprecated, record it in the CHANGELOG, open a deprecation RFC, and add a deprecation banner to the Storybook docs with suggested migration alternatives.
- Minimum deprecation window: 90 days from public announcement to removal for tokens/components with measurable usage. For low-usage internals a shorter window (30 days) may be acceptable with org-wide notice.
- Telemetry & usage checks: before removal, run an inventory (static analysis + runtime telemetry where available) to estimate usage and create a migration plan.
- Migration aids: provide codemods, mapping tables (old -> new tokens), and a short migration guide in the docs.
- Fallback behavior: until removal, the deprecated token/component remains functional and emits a console warning when used in dev builds.
- Removal gate: removal requires an approved RFC, sign-off by DS lead and a release manager, and a published migration guide + codemod.

Operational/maintenance rules:
- Token audit cadence: quarterly automated audits to detect duplicate or near-duplicate tokens and orphaned tokens not referenced by components or docs.
- Component health dashboard: weekly checks for Storybook regression failures, visual diffs, and bundle size impact.
- Ownership rota: designate 1 owner per major component group (buttons, form controls, tables, charts, tokens) and rotate on-call weekly for triage of DS regressions.

Communication & rollout:
- Public changelog entry for each accepted RFC that affects public API or tokens.
- Slack #design-system channel for RFC announcements with link to RFC + expected timeline.
- Email digest for enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) when deprecations affect compatibility or require manual migration.

Examples & links (placeholders):
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
- RFC template & tracker: https://docs.internal.redwood.com/design/rfcs
- Storybook: https://ds.redwood-inference.internal/storybook
- Migration codemod examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/tree/main/ds

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Publish a one-page governance playbook in the design docs (Confluence/Drive)
- Add DS PR template checks to the repo CI (block merge if template not filled)
- Create a minimal RFC template in docs and a sample RFC for a token rename scenario
- Implement a deprecation banner component in Storybook and add to docs

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: rushed removals break customer apps. Mitigation: enforce minimum deprecation windows, telemetry checks, and codemods.
- Risk: friction deters contributors. Mitigation: clear small-PR guidance, templates, and automation (CI checks + codemods).
